story.head: Who blinks first?
paras: The Golden Knights won the teams’ first meeting this season, 6-2 in Vegas on Oct 17. The Golden Knights (9-5-1) lost 5-2 to New Jersey on Friday, and the Penguins (5-6-2) lost 4-3 in overtime to Utah on Thursday. The Golden Knights played last night, and the Penguins are rested. Going in, the Golden Knights are second in the Pacific (tied for fourth in the NHL) and the Penguins sixth in the Metropolitan (tied for 24th).

The Golden Knights have played better than their record (.633) says: their chances are worth about .691, and their goaltending has held them back. So have the Penguins (.462 on chances worth .559), where losses in one-goal games have held them back.

The Golden Knights draw more penalties than they take (1st), but have had shaky goaltending (31st). They also have the league’s best penalty kill (1st), so the Penguins’ struggling power play gets a tough test from their penalty killers. The Pens sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (lowest), get more of their shots from in close than anyone (1st) and rarely throw hits (lowest). The Penguins’ good looks will be harder to come by against the Golden Knights.

Jack Eichel (7 G / 13 A / 20 P in 15 GP) leads the Golden Knights in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, and Mark Stone (9 G / 8 A / 17 P in 15 GP) has a team-high nine goals, tied for seventh in the NHL. The Penguins’ scoring runs through Erik Karlsson (2 G / 11 A / 13 P in 13 GP), and Nick Robertson (6 G / 0 A / 6 P in 13 GP) has a team-high six goals.
Adin Hill (5-2-0 / .891 SV% in 7 GS) will likely start for Vegas, and Artūrs Šilovs (5-3-1 / .889 SV% in 9 GS) for Pittsburgh.

items.text: The Golden Knights have been without Parker Wotherspoon and Victor Olofsson for several games.
The Penguins are newly without Evgeni Malkin and Bryan Rust, and have been without Trevor van Riemsdyk since Oct 9.
Mitch Marner has two goals on chances worth about 3.8 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
Jérémy Lauzon and Declan Carlile fought the last time these two met.
